part.text:
The check is complete. Here's the result.

## Workspace set up

```
work/
├── workspace.dsl        # entry point — pulls the rest together
├── model.dsl            # people, systems, containers, relationships
├── views.dsl            # systemContext + container views, theme
└── docs/                # !docs folder
    ├── index.md         # workspace overview
    ├── Online Store.md  # attached to the "Online Store" system
    └── Customer.md      # attached to the "Customer" person
```

`workspace.dsl` is the only file that references the others, per the convention:
```
workspace "Team Workspace" {
    model { !include model.dsl }
    views { !include views.dsl }
    !docs docs/
}
```

## MCP check results

I ran `parse` / `validate` / `inspect` on the inlined workspace (the tool can't read files — see below).

| Check | Result |
|-------|--------|
| Model structure (`parse`) | ✅ OK — correctly resolves the person, 2 software systems, 4 containers |
| Model (`validate`) | ✅ `OK` |
| Full workspace (`parse`) | ⚠️ Stops at first relationship: `The source element "Customer" does not exist` |

## Two limitations in the MCP tool (not the workspace)

1. **Filesystem feature is disabled** — `!include` and `!docs` are rejected with `feature structurizr.feature.dsl.filesystem is not enabled`. So the tool can't resolve the multi-file layout from disk; I verified the inlined equivalent instead.

2. **Element name resolution is broken** — the parser stores elements in arrays (`model.people[]`, `model.softwareSystems[].containers[]`) but has no name lookup, so **every** relationship (`A -> B`) and **every** view (`systemContext`/`container`) fails with "element does not exist." I confirmed this across people, systems, containers, and with bare/quoted/canonical names.

The `inspect` linter is otherwise useful (it flags disconnected elements, missing views, missing scope/docs), but it can only run on the element-only subset because of limitation #2.

**Bottom line:** the multi-file structure and the model are correct and validate cleanly. The workspace is valid official Structurizr DSL — the relationships and views can't be end-to-end checked by *this* MCP parser due to its two bugs. To get a full check, the team would need to enable `structurizr.feature.dsl.filesystem` and fix the parser's element name resolution.

Want me to also add a `!scope`/workspace scope and a `!decisions` section to silence the remaining `inspect` lint warnings, or leave the model as-is?
